body.statement: There are constants \(C<\infty\) and \(n_0\), depending only on \(\alpha\) and the fixed indices \(B_A,B_Y,\beta,R_f,R_q,\kappa,q_e,M_e,\nu_0,c_0,p_{\min},|\mathcal X|\), such that the deterministic construction \(\mathfrak H^{\mathrm{up}}\) yields jointly sample-and-index measurable finite endpoints with \(L_n(a)\le U_n(a)\) for every \(a\in I\) almost surely, \(\mathcal C_n\in\mathfrak B_{n,\alpha}\), and \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal M}E_{P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}}[W_n]\le Cr_n\) for every \(n\ge n_0\). Coverage follows on \(\mathcal E_{n,\alpha}\). On every realized regular-count sample \(\min_xn_x\ge np_{\min}/2\), the width is at most \(Cr_n\) regardless of coverage-event failure; clipping bounds it by \(2B_Y\) on the exponentially rare count failure. The multinomial coordinate contributes \(O([\log(|\mathcal X|/\alpha)/n]^{1/2})=o(r_n)\) to the diameter.
body.justification: The causal and probabilistic reductions are complete conditional on analytic-sieve feasibility and stability; those deterministic premises remain unproved.
body.gap: No claimed comparator supplies the missing uniform marked-quotient stability result for two blind asymmetric error factors.
body.consumer: Completion would provide whole-curve uncertainty for the Melaku--Shi (2026) two-recall diet--mortality analysis.

obligation.what_is_open: The upper theorem now has its pointwise causal bridge, but it still requires the feasible constrained-sieve embedding and the deterministic analytic stability bound from \(\mathrm{lem{:}analytic\text{-}sieve\text{-}stability}\).
obligation.obstruction: Without those deterministic assertions, the true approximating tuple is not known to belong to \(\Theta_{n,\alpha}\), and empirical residual control cannot bound the diameter of the profiled ADRF set. Thus neither uniform coverage of the stated construction nor its \(r_n\) width follows yet.
obligation.attempted: The coverage and expected-width reduction was completed conditional on feasible embedding and the inverse modulus, including the regular-count split, the \(o(r_n)\) multinomial term, and the exponentially small count-failure remainder.
obligation.partial_result:
The causal bridge needed for coverage is supplied by \(\mathrm{thm{:}adrf\text{-}id}\). Conditional on the two unresolved deterministic assertions in \(\mathrm{lem{:}analytic\text{-}sieve\text{-}stability}\), the rest of the upper theorem follows. On \(\mathcal E_{n,\alpha}\), a feasible approximating tuple \(\bar\theta\) satisfying \(\|\mu_{\bar\theta}-\mu\|_{L^\infty(I)}\le b_{\mu,n}\) and the profiled endpoint definitions imply \(L_n(a)\le\mu(a)\le U_n(a)\) for every \(a\in I\). On the regular-count event, the deterministic feasible-set diameter and the two endpoint inflations give
\[
 W_n\le C\left\{K_n^{1/2-\beta}+\sqrt{\lambda_n/n}\right\}\le C'r_n,
\]
because \(b_{\mu,n}=O(K_n^{1/2-\beta})\) and \(\sqrt{\lambda_n/n}=o(r_n)\). On count failure, \(W_n\le2B_Y\), while \(\mathrm{lem{:}mass\text{-}confidence}\) bounds its probability by \(|\mathcal X|e^{-np_{\min}/8}\). Consequently,
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal M}E_{P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\otimes n}}[W_n]
 \le C'r_n+2B_Y|\mathcal X|e^{-np_{\min}/8}
 =O(r_n).
\]
Thus the remaining obstruction is deterministic analytic stability and feasible sieve embedding, not causal identification or an additional probabilistic argument.
